summary: SIP module is shallow relative to the surface. OPTIONS + REGISTER-based extension enumeration + digest challenge parse + internal-IP leak detection + MD5-only advertisement flag. No auth attempt against enumerated extensions (no svcrack-style), no INVITE toll-fraud test, no OPTIONS to a specific extension to catch alwaysauthreject=no-for-existing-user, no CVE mapping despite the vendor slug already being computed, no SIP-over-TLS (5061) TLS-side probe. sip_ext_enum reaches T2 for the seen_ok=200 branch (unauth REGISTER accepted).

findings.title_pattern: SIP endpoint discloses server / realm via unauth OPTIONS
findings.tier_evidence: Server / realm / Allow are pure fingerprint bytes.
findings.promotion_notes: Once vendor slug is computed, feed to CVE mapper (Asterisk AMI CVEs, Kamailio SDP parse RCE etc). Currently vendor is stored (pr['vendor']) but no CVE mapping table exists yet.

findings.tier_evidence: Real 401/407 vs 404 asymmetry observed on REGISTER; when seen_ok=200 a REGISTER completed unauth = T2 primitive (register-and-place-calls). Extension list captured.
findings.promotion_notes: Chain svcrack-style bounded password spray against the enumerated extensions using known_passwords once shared. Or on seen_ok, actually place an INVITE to prove toll-fraud (destructive, gate).
findings.tester_next_step: svcrack.py -u <ext> -d rockyou.txt <ip>:<port>; on hit hydra -l <ext> -P wordlist sip://<ip>. For seen_ok=200 branches, register a soft-phone (linphone --sip <ext>@<ip>) and try an outbound call to a controlled number.

findings.title_pattern: SIP response discloses internal IP address
findings.tier_evidence: Received/Contact private IP different from reached IP is deterministic leak proof.
findings.promotion_notes: Add the leaked internal IP to known_hosts so downstream port scans target it on the far side of a NAT/SBC pivot.
findings.tester_next_step: sipsak -vv -s sip:<ip>:<port>; feed the leaked internal IP to arp/scan (once inside).

findings.title_pattern: SIP Digest authentication offers MD5 only (no RFC 8760 SHA-256)
findings.promotion_notes: Wait for or induce a real client REGISTER response to build a hashcat 11400 line and crack (already suggested in tester text). Alternatively, run svcrack against a discovered extension.
findings.tester_next_step: tcpdump -i <iface> 'udp port 5060' -A | tee sip.log; grep -A20 'REGISTER sip' sip.log | grep -oE 'response="[a-f0-9]+"'; assemble $sip$***realm***nonce***md5***user***uri***qop***response and feed hashcat -m 11400.
